title: Federal money passed from one City-paid organization to another
question: Where does a City-paid organization hold a federal grant and pass part of it to another City-paid organization, outside any City process?
finding: 19 pairs, $7.4 million in all, in the federal subaward register for fiscal 2019 to 2026. The largest: American Institutes For Research to Wested ($4.2 million, 2018-2024, Second Chance Act Reentry Initiative); Mission Economic Development Agency to Open Door Legal ($1.0 million, 2025, Eviction Protection Grant Program); Public Health Institute to Richmond Area Multi-Services Inc ($617,134, 2022, Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Projects of Regio); Enterprise Community Partners Inc. to Mission Economic Development Agency ($565,000, 2020-2026, Section 4 Capacity Building for Community Development and Af). 1 register row was set aside because its amount repeats its own subaward number and is larger than the whole prime award: an entry error in the source, not a payment.
how: USAspending subawards to San Francisco recipients where both the prime recipient and the subrecipient normalise to a profiled City-paid organization. City payments are the payment-table totals for the same fiscal years. Shared leaders are read from grant_chains (the same officer or director on both tax returns).
limits: A national intermediary passing capacity-building money to local housing groups is the purpose of that federal programme. The question each row raises is narrower: the City pays the recipient for work of the same kind in the same years (eviction defence, for one), and neither funder’s file shows the other’s budget. The subrecipient is tied by name plus its San Francisco address in the register; the award holder by name alone, and for it the records do not show whether it is the same organisation or two with the same name (the register’s entity number against the City’s supplier file would settle it). The subrecipient’s two budgets would show whether the same staff are charged twice.
